data.narrative:
Oxford Quantum Circuits is a Series C quantum computing company that has raised $350M to date. The valuation universe comprises 11 peers across quantum computing—three public companies (IonQ, Rigetti, D-Wave) and eight private firms including Quantinuum and Infleqtion—though the private peer set at OQC's specific stage and tier lacks sufficient depth for reliable median benchmarking.

Stage-progression methodology is the primary applicable lens here. Using total capital raised ($350M) as a valuation proxy and applying a 1.7x step-up multiplier typical of Series C advancement yields $595M. This method assumes OQC will progress to the next institutional funding round at a markup consistent with historical quantum computing financings. Peer-median analysis was not applicable; while five quantum computing companies exist in the dataset, filtering for same-stage and adjacent-stage peers with comparable valuation tiers produced fewer than three datapoints, rendering sector-wide medians unreliably broad.

The triangulation supports a median valuation of $595M, with a low-end estimate of $506M and high-end of $684M, reflecting ±15% confidence bounds around the stage-progression result. Key uncertainties include the representativeness of the 1.7x multiplier to OQC's specific investor composition and competitive positioning within quantum, and the absence of direct peer comparables at Series C in this emerging sector. Additional data on recent Series C+ quantum financings would narrow this range materially.
